name: Napa Valley Cassoulet
steps: put beans in stock pot and add water to cover twice the height of the beans. add bay leaf, diced shallot, garlic, thyme, and parsley. bring to a boil then simmer for 2 hours.
turn off heat, add some salt to taste, and stir. drain the beans.
preheat oven to 350f.
melt 2 tbsp of duck fat in a pan. add garlic, celery, onion, and carrot. saute until the vegetables are tender.
transfer vegetables to a roasting pan. drizzle the tomatoes and their juice over the vegetables.
add pork chunks to pan.
sprinkle thyme over the vegetables. melt some duck fat in pan and add some white wine. drizzle mixture over the vegetables.
cover roasting pan with aluminum foil. bake for 2.5 hours.
remove roasting pan. transfer pork to a container. drain liquid from pan into a separate bowl.
puree vegetables in food processor. skim off any fat from the surface and then stir the puree into the beans.
combine broth, ham hock, thyme, bay leaf, and diced shallot in a saucepan over high heat. bring to a boil then simmer for 1 hour
remove meat from ham hock and discard the fat, bone, and skin. add the meat to the reserved pork chunks.
set oven heat to 325f.
remove meat from duck legs, discard the bones, and set meat aside.
poke sausages with a fork a few times. poach them in boiling water for 10 minutes.
brown sausages in a pan using some duck fat. set sausage aside.
add one third of beans to bottom of a deep earthenware pot. add pieces of pork and duck evenly. add another third of the beans and add sausage evenly.
add remaining beans evenly on top. add enough broth to fill below the rim.
mix panko with some melted duck fat and toss to coat. pour panko over the top layer of beans.
bake for 1.5 hours. remove cassoulet from oven. break the top crust and if the broth has evaporated, add more. add any remaining melted duck fat.
bake for another 1.5 hours, or until juices bubble around the edges and a golden crust has formed.
